summary: The council flow tracks skills/council.md almost line for line: phases, lenses, review questions, verdict sections and rules all have source text. Two wording issues remain: 'Three questions, about 200 words each' misreads a per-review limit as per-question, and the brief's risk states a consequence the source does not. The optional Jev-accelerated mode and the batching rule for fewer than five slots are not shown.

code.overview: The council runs entirely as agent-followed prose: framing the brief, spawning the five advisors, anonymizing for peer review and writing the verdict have no code behind them, and the optional Jev mode has no script in this repo either. The only council-specific code is scripts/test-council-skill.sh, which greps skills/council.md so the key instructions cannot be deleted unnoticed, plus the thin wrapper that carries the trigger description. That test runs through npm test (test:shell) in CI; it checks the wording of the skill, not how a council actually behaves.

refs.anchor: description: Run a high-stakes decision through a council of five persona-diverse advisors (Contrarian, First-Principles, Expansionist, Outsider, Executor) in parallel, then anonymized peer review, then a chairman synthesis of where they agree, clash, and what to do. Use for real tradeoffs ("council this", "pressure-test this", "should I X or Y"), not factual or low-stakes questions.
refs.title: Claude wrapper: the trigger description
refs.explain: The frontmatter holds one description line that names the five advisors, the three rounds, and the trigger phrases 'council this', 'pressure-test this' and 'should I X or Y'. It also says not to use it for factual or low-stakes questions. The last line includes the canonical body skills/council.md.
refs.why: This description is what the harness reads to decide whether an owner's question should start a council. The decision itself is the model's judgement; there is no code that classifies the question.

refs.anchor: && ok "when-not-to-use guard present" || fail "when-not-to-use guard missing"
refs.title: test: the when-not-to-use guard stays in the skill
refs.explain: It greps skills/council.md, ignoring case, for 'not use', 'do not use', 'factual' or 'low-stakes'. A match counts as a pass and no match counts as a failure.
refs.why: The first stage says factual and low-stakes questions skip the council. This test only pins that the skill still says so; it would pass if any one of those words remained.

refs.title: test: council is wired into wrapper, manifest and RESOLVER
refs.explain: It checks that the Claude wrapper includes skills/council.md. It checks that each of the five council files is listed in .github/scaffold-files.txt. It checks that RESOLVER.md has a row for council.
refs.why: An owner can only reach the council if the skill is routed and shipped. Without the RESOLVER row or manifest entries the trigger phrases would lead nowhere in a consumer repo.

refs.anchor: && ok "advisor persona present: $persona" || fail "advisor persona missing: $persona"
refs.title: test: all five advisor lenses are named
refs.explain: It loops over the five persona names and greps skills/council.md for each one. Each name found is a pass; a missing name is a failure.
refs.why: The Five advisors stage depends on five fixed lenses that are built to disagree. This stops an edit from dropping one of them from the skill text.

refs.anchor: && ok "isolated-subagent execution described" || fail "isolated-subagent model not described"
refs.title: test: parallel, isolated, peer-reviewed, chaired
refs.explain: Four greps over skills/council.md, in order: 'parallel' or 'concurrent'; 'peer review' or 'anonymize'; 'chairman'; and 'isolated subagent' or 'isolated context'. Each is counted as a pass or a failure.
refs.why: These are the mechanics of the advisors, peer review and chairman stages. The test proves the instructions exist in the skill; it cannot check that a real run spawned isolated subagents or shuffled the labels.

refs.anchor: && ok "output: agreements section" || fail "output missing agreements section"
refs.title: test: the verdict keeps its required sections
refs.explain: It greps skills/council.md for 'Where the council agrees', then 'Where the council clashes', then 'one thing to do first' or 'do first'. Each is a pass or a failure.
refs.why: The chairman must show agreement, real disagreement and a single first step. This pins those headings in the output template so the verdict format is not thinned out by an edit.

promptOnly.what: The main agent scans the repo for context and writes a neutral brief with the decision, options, constraints, success criteria and the trade space; nothing checks the brief.

The agent relabels the five answers A to E in random order and gives them to five reviewers with three questions; no code does the shuffle or the dispatch, and the test only checks that the skill text mentions peer review.
